# Start here

Pick a cup: follow a path, grab a quick read, or start with the basics.

## Learning paths

Read each path in order; every step builds on the one before.

### Generative AI · 6 steps · 58 min

1. [Compute-Bound vs Memory-Bandwidth-Bound](/fields/generative-ai/llm-inference-performance/compute-bound-vs-memory-bound.md) — Why a 3x faster GPU can give you 1.6x - arithmetic intensity, the ridge point and the roofline, explained with a pizza kitchen and two lines of arithmetic. *(intermediate · 9 min)*
2. [LLM Inference on the Roofline](/fields/generative-ai/llm-inference-performance/llm-inference-on-the-roofline.md) — Why your chatbot reads a novel-length prompt in a blink but types its answer like a tired intern - prefill, decode, batching and the KV cache on the roofline. *(intermediate · 9 min)*
3. [Sizing a 70B Model with a Pencil](/fields/generative-ai/llm-inference-performance/sizing-a-70b-model.md) — A live whiteboard walk-through - Llama 2 70B on 8xH100, from "does it fit?" to the exact token-rate ceilings at batch 1 and batch 64, using only a datasheet. *(intermediate · 9 min)*
4. [Optimizations, Mapped to the Roofline](/fields/generative-ai/llm-inference-performance/optimizations-on-the-roofline.md) — Five proposals in one meeting, one roofline to judge them - batching, PagedAttention, quantization, tensor parallelism, FlashAttention, speculative decoding, disaggregation, and how to measure. *(intermediate · 12 min)*
5. [2:4 Sparsity: Half the Weights, Not Half the Time](/fields/generative-ai/llm-inference-performance/structured-sparsity.md) — How NVIDIA's 2:4 structured sparsity works, what it really saves (44% of weight bytes, not 50%), and why its doubled TFLOPS help prefill while decode only feels the byte savings. *(intermediate · 9 min)*
6. [Sparsity vs Quantization: Who Pays, and Who Wins](/fields/generative-ai/llm-inference-performance/sparsity-vs-quantization.md) — What it costs to prune an LLM to 2:4, how much accuracy goes with it, how it compares with FP8 and 4-bit quantization, and why the usual order is quantize first, sparsify second. *(intermediate · 10 min)*

### Systems and HPC · 8 steps · 62 min

1. [Containers 101](/fields/libraries-frameworks-containers/101-containers.md) *(8 min)*
2. [Kubernetes in Five Nouns, Explained Like You Just Inherited the Cluster](/fields/devops/kubernetes/kubernetes-in-five-nouns.md) — The five Kubernetes nouns (node, pod, namespace, event, API server) explained through HPC analogies, for someone who just inherited a cluster. *(advanced · 8 min)*
3. [Build a Two-Node Kubernetes Lab on Your Laptop (and Survive the DNS Pothole)](/fields/devops/kubernetes/build-a-two-node-k3s-lab.md) — Build a two-VM Kubernetes lab on your laptop with Vagrant, libvirt and k3s, and dodge the DNS and network potholes. *(intermediate · 7 min)*
4. [Fake GPUs in Kubernetes: Learn GPU Scheduling Without Owning a GPU](/fields/devops/kubernetes/fake-gpus-in-kubernetes.md) — Patch a node with a fake nvidia.com/gpu counter to learn GPU scheduling without owning a GPU. *(intermediate · 6 min)*
5. [Broken Pods: A Rogues' Gallery (and the One Command That Catches Them All)](/fields/devops/kubernetes/broken-pods-rogues-gallery.md) — How to recognise CrashLoop, OOMKilled, ImagePull and Pending pods by reading status, events and previous logs. *(intermediate · 6 min)*
6. [Booked Is Not Busy: GPU Allocation vs Utilization](/fields/devops/kubernetes/gpu-allocation-vs-utilization.md) — The scheduler knows who has booked the GPUs, not whether they’re busy, so use kubectl for the first question and DCGM-style telemetry for the second. *(intermediate · 7 min)*
7. [The Cluster That Passed Every Test Except the One That Mattered](/fields/devops/kubernetes/nvidia-cluster-readiness-engine.md) — Even when traditional monitoring tools show all GPUs and networks operating normally, subtle bottlenecks—like a single slow GPU or a degraded network link—can silently drag down the performance of an *(intermediate · 10 min)*
8. [Singularity](/fields/libraries-frameworks-containers/101-singularity.md) *(10 min)*

### Deep Learning · 3 steps · 39 min

1. [Deep Learning Basics](/fields/deep-learning/concepts/basics.md) — Neurons, loss and cost, and the common activation functions, explained from first principles. *(beginner · 30 min)*
2. [Sequence Models](/fields/deep-learning/concepts/sequence-models.md) — How models handle ordered data like text, from RNNs and LSTMs to transformers and LLMs. *(intermediate · 6 min)*
3. [Encoder-Decoder for Machine Translation](/fields/generative-ai/machine-translator/encoder-decoder.md) — The encoder-decoder idea behind neural machine translation, with a basic seq2seq model. *(intermediate · 3 min)*

### Systems and HPC · 3 steps · 28 min

1. [Four Ways to Ask Slurm for Mixed GPUs](/fields/schedulers/slurm-mixed-gpus/four-ways-to-mix-gpus.md) — Typed GRES, constraint operators, heterogeneous jobs and heterogeneous steps - what each one actually allocates, and the one-character constraint that mixes GPU types by accident. *(intermediate · 9 min)*
2. [Why Mixed-GPU Training Disappoints](/fields/schedulers/slurm-mixed-gpus/why-mixed-training-disappoints.md) — Why 8 H100s plus 8 A100s train like 16 A100s, which H100 features the A100s switch off, and what co-scheduling a heterogeneous job costs you in the queue. *(intermediate · 9 min)*
3. [Where Heterogeneous Jobs Shine](/fields/schedulers/slurm-mixed-gpus/where-hetjobs-shine.md) — The workloads where mixing GPU types in one Slurm job is exactly right, how admins should label and guard a multi-generation cluster, a decision table, and the interview answer. *(intermediate · 10 min)*

### Systems and HPC · 6 steps · 64 min

1. [How GPU Memory Fails, and Why You Can See It Coming](/fields/system-administration/gpu-failure-prediction/what-fails-and-what-warns.md) — How ECC, row remapping and error containment work on NVIDIA GPUs, why memory errors repeat and cluster, and the error ladder that makes failure predictable. *(intermediate · 11 min)*
2. [Reading the GPU's Vital Signs](/fields/system-administration/gpu-failure-prediction/collecting-the-signals.md) — The telemetry concepts behind GPU failure prediction - counters, gauges and events, volatile versus persistent, in-band versus out-of-band - and the ways each one misleads. *(intermediate · 9 min)*
3. [From Signals to Decisions](/fields/system-administration/gpu-failure-prediction/rules-that-predict.md) — How to design GPU failure rules - state, event and trend rules, personal baselines, persistence, noise floors and action tiers - and the traps that make rules silently fail. *(advanced · 10 min)*
4. [Acting Without Making It Worse](/fields/system-administration/gpu-failure-prediction/from-alert-to-drain.md) — The principles of safe automated response to GPU failure predictions - reversibility, drain semantics, blast radius, drain budgets, staged rollout and rollback. *(advanced · 9 min)*
5. [Is the Prediction Any Good?](/fields/system-administration/gpu-failure-prediction/scoring-and-backtesting.md) — How to judge GPU failure predictions - base rates, precision, recall, lead time, horizons, label quality, leakage and drift - and when a learned model is worth it. *(advanced · 10 min)*
6. [Runbook: Deploying GPU Failure Prediction End to End](/fields/system-administration/gpu-failure-prediction/runbook.md) — The hands-on companion to the series - counters file, node checks, tested Prometheus rules, Alertmanager routing, a guarded Slurm drain hook and a backtest, step by step. *(advanced · 15 min)*

2. [PyTorch DDP](/fields/libraries-frameworks-containers/102-pytorch-ddp.md) *(1 min)*

Sessions and Two Walls](/programming/local-app-accounts/sessions-and-two-walls.md) — How an app remembers who is signed in, why remember-me stores a fingerprint instead of a token, and why authorization needs one check at the door and another at the data. *(intermediate · 6 min)*

### Systems and HPC · 10 steps · 85 min

1. [Why Your Cluster Needs a Bouncer](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/why-node-health-check.md) — One broken node can eat a whole queue of jobs; this is what NHC is, how it decides a node is sick, and how it tells the scheduler. *(beginner · 7 min)*
2. [Build and Install NHC](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/build-and-install.md) — Get NHC onto your nodes from a release RPM, the release tarball or the Git tree, run its unit tests and know where every file lands. *(beginner · 5 min)*
3. [Writing nhc.conf That Actually Fits Your Cluster](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/writing-nhc-conf.md) — The config syntax, match strings, variables and contexts, plus copy-ready starter configs for CPU, GPU and login nodes. *(intermediate · 8 min)*
4. [Plugging NHC into Slurm (and Friends)](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/slurm-integration.md) — The three slurm.conf lines, which node states to check, timeouts that don't fight each other, prolog and epilog patterns, reboots, plus PBS and cron. *(intermediate · 7 min)*
5. [Rolling NHC Out to a Fleet Without Draining Everything](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/rollout-at-scale.md) — A dry-run, canary, enforce plan for deploying NHC or a new nhc.conf to hundreds of nodes, with a circuit breaker for bad pushes. *(intermediate · 6 min)*
6. [Writing Your Own NHC Checks](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/custom-checks.md) — Build a site .nhc module the way upstream does, with cached data, clear failure messages, fast bash, and practical GPU checks. *(advanced · 7 min)*
7. [Auto-Remediation: From Detected to Fixed, Safely](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/auto-remediation.md) — Turn NHC drains into automatic fixes with an escalation ladder, built-in fix actions, a node-doctor loop on the controller, and guard rails against reboot storms. *(advanced · 8 min)*
8. [NHC Troubleshooting: Symptom First](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/troubleshooting.md) — Symptom-first fixes for false drains, nodes that never resume, slurmd that won't register, timeouts, hanging df, and checks that pass by hand but fail under Slurm. *(intermediate · 8 min)*
9. [Architecture-Driven NHC: Generate Health Checks from Your Cluster's Definition](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/architecture-driven-nhc.md) — Describe your cluster's architecture once in YAML, generate every NHC config from it, cross-check it against slurm.conf, and prove the result with real NHC before it ships. *(advanced · 12 min)*
10. [Case Study: "Build Us an NHC", From a Vague Ask to a Validated Proposal](/fields/system-administration/node-health-check/case-study-build-me-an-nhc.md) — A client asks for an NHC for their DGX H100 and AMD EPYC Slurm cluster; the discovery questions, first proposal, validation against vendor specs, and the final answer. *(advanced · 17 min)*
